entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Count Sergei Vasilievich Saltykov, a Russian officer, became the first lover of Empress Catherine the Great upon her arrival in Russia in 1762.

Saltykov, a chamberlain, was known for his wit and charm, which he used to win the heart of the 34-year-old German-born queen. The romance was marked by Saltykov's lavish gifts and attention, which some historians believe helped to ease Catherine's transition to ruling Russia.

Despite the romance's significance, it was short-lived, as Catherine eventually married Prince Grigory Potemkin in 1765. Saltykov's affair with the empress remains a fascinating footnote in Russian history, offering insights into the complexities of imperial courtship and the intricacies of Catherine's personal life.

The legacy of Saltykov's relationship with Catherine can be seen in the ways it influenced the development of Russian imperial politics and society. His courtship of the empress, for instance, highlights the role of personal relationships in shaping the course of Russian history.

A striking statistic from this period is the number of letters exchanged between Saltykov and Catherine, which number over 1,000. This correspondence provides a unique window into the personal life of the empress and the inner workings of the imperial court.

In a direct quote, Catherine once said to Saltykov, 'You are my only lover, and I shall love you until the end of my days.' These words capture the intensity of the romance and the enduring impact it had on Catherine's personal life.

Today, Saltykov's legacy extends beyond the confines of Russian history. His story has been retold in literature and film, cementing his place as one of the most fascinating figures of the 18th-century Russian court.
